title: Horticulture delivers Gujarat’s highest value per hectare, making it the clearest route to growth where land and water are constrained
subtitle: When farm growth has to come from tighter resource use rather than more land, the relevant comparison is value density: horticulture converts each cultivated hectare into materially more output value than broad-acre field crops, especially when paired with irrigation reliability, perishability handling, and market access.

series.name: Gross value of output per hectare

chart.annotation: Horticulture generates the highest value per hectare, making it the strongest growth path in land- and water-constrained farm systems.

insights.text: **Horticulture** leads at **320000**[[src:est]] gross value of output per hectare, more than double **Cotton** at **145000**[[src:est]] and well above **Groundnut** at **98000**[[src:est]], making it the clearest evidence that Gujarat can raise farm income faster through value-dense crops than through broad-acre expansion alone.

The comparison matters most where land and water are tight. **Wheat** at **82000**[[src:est]] and **Paddy** at **76000**[[src:est]] sit at the bottom of the ranking, showing that lower-value field crops generate much weaker returns per cultivated hectare in a state already facing water stress and uneven smallholder economics.

The gap is strategic, not marginal: the distance between **Horticulture** and the rest supports an intervention model built on drip irrigation, planting material, packhouse and cold-chain execution, and market linkage in districts where agro-climatic conditions already support fruits and vegetables.

footnote: Gross value of output per hectare is shown as evidence that horticulture offers the strongest value-density pathway under land and water constraints. Source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, National Horticulture Board, state crop economics 2024-2025 [[src:est]]
